guidelines: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 804: Physical Activity and Exercise During Pregnancy and the Postpartum Period
instruction: Identify the correct muscles: Imagine trying to stop the flow of urine or prevent passing gas without clenching your buttocks or thighs.
Contract and lift the pelvic floor inward for 3-5 seconds, then completely relax for 5 seconds.
Integrate with diaphragmatic breathing: exhale as you lift/contract, inhale as you gently release.
precautions: Do not practice Kegels while actually urinating to avoid incomplete bladder emptying or urinary tract infections.

guidelines: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 202: Physical Activity and Exercise in Pregnancy
recommendations: Target 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity per week (e.g., brisk walking, prenatal swimming, stationary cycling, modified yoga).
Use the 'Talk Test': You should be able to hold a conversation while exercising without becoming breathless.
Avoid supine exercises (lying flat on back) after the 1st trimester to prevent aortocaval compression by the gravid uterus.
Avoid contact sports, hot yoga, or activities with high fall risk.
redFlags: Stop immediately and seek medical evaluation if you experience vaginal bleeding, amniotic fluid leakage, regular painful contractions, calf swelling/pain, or chest pain.
